title.narrative: DKT- Hållbar kapacitetsuppbyggnad av SRHR i nordöstra Kongo
DKT-Building Sustainable SRHR Capacity in Northeast DRC

description.narrative:
DKT is one of the only three importers of Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) products in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). DKT provides access to a wide range of SRH products to combat unintended pregnancies, transmitted infections and avert unsafe abortions, with a focus on under-served populations. This contribution will expand DKTs sustainable social marketing activities in North and South Kivu to increase demand, empower community providers to increase acceptance of SRH products, and provide capacity building to serve victims of Gender-Based Violence (GBV), during 2021-2023.
North and South Kivu has been marred by years of armed conflict, where sexual violence by armed groups or forces on women or girls (“rape as a weapon of war”) has been rampant, and where the conflicts have disrupted health and education systems. Consequently, donor responses to the humanitarian situation have been fluctuant, depending on crisis and donor priorities. This has had negative impact on sustainable SRH service and provision models as well as durable capacity building of health systems and response.
The Embassy deems it necessary to continue supporting organisations working on strengthening Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), and response to sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV).The expected results for the DKT project, with the funding available, is to provide a long-term solution to SRH by expanding service provision through community-based distribution, and by training a cohort of providers to offer commodities in North and South Kivu. More specifically DKT is expected to: • Strengthen the province's distribution system to ensure a permanent presence of contraceptive and Post Abortion Care (PAC) and Medical Abortion products. • Empower community-based providers to work within their communities on SRH information and awareness raising. • Train health care providers on how to serve survivors of (S)GBV, address taboos around sexuality, and demystify cultural preferences for large families.
This will be done by: • Leveraging the existing private infrastructure, including clinics, pharmacies, shops and community health networks. • Building a sustainable network of community nurses, midwives and community health care providers by training them on the provision of SRH services. • Training 300 health care provides on the provision of SRH services including services to victims of GBV.

DKT är en av bara tre importörer av SRH-produkter (sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa) i Demokratiska Republiken Kongo (DRK). DKT erbjuder ett brett utbud av SRH-produkter för att motverka oönskade graviditeter, könssjukdomar och osäkra aborter. Insatsen syftar till att utöka DKTs hållbara sociala marknadsföringsaktiviteter i norra och södra Kivu, för att öka efterfrågan på SRH- produkter, öka acceptansen av SRH-produkter genom att arbeta med samhällsleverantörer, samt tillhandahålla kapacitetsuppbyggnad för hantering av könsbaserat våld, under perioden 2021-2023.
Nord- och Syd Kivu har präglats av år av väpnade konflikter, där sexuellt våld utövats av väpnade grupper eller styrkor mot kvinnor och flickor. Våldtäkt har använts som ett krigsvapen och konflikterna har även haft förödande konsekvenser på hälso- och utbildningsystemen. Givarstöd till den humanitära situationen har varit fluktuerande, beroende på kris och givarprioriteringar. Detta har haft negativ inverkan på hållbara SRH-tjänster samt kapacitetsuppbyggnad av hälsosystem och respons. Ambassaden anser att det är nödvändigt att fortsätta stödja organisationer som arbetar med att stärka sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR), och arbetet mot sexuellt och könsbaserat våld. De förväntade resultaten från DKT-projektet, med den tillgängliga finansieringen, är att tillhandahålla en långsiktig lösning för SRHR, genom att utöka utbudet av SRH produkter och tjänster, genom samhällsbaserad distribution, samt utbildning av en grupp leverantörer som kan erbjuda produkter och SRHR-vård i norra och södra Kivu.
Mer specifikt förväntas DKT: • Stärka provinsens distributionssystem för att säkerställa en permanent tillgång till preventivmedel och abortvård/läkemedel. • Möjliggöra för lokala leverantörer att arbeta inom sina samhällen med SRH-information och kunskapsbildande. • Utbilda vårdpersonal i hur man hanterar fall av sexuellt eller könsrelaterat våld, men även hur de kan hantera existerande tabun och stigman kring sexualitet och föreställningen om den kulturella vikten att ha flertal barn.
Detta kommer att göras genom att: • Utnyttja den befintliga privata hälsoinfrastrukturen, det vill säga kliniker, apotek, butiker och olika hälsonätverk. • Bygga ett hållbart nätverk av sjuksköterskor, barnmorskor och vårdpersonal i samhället, genom utbildning och tillhandahållande av SRH-tjänster. • Utbilda 300 hälso- och sjukvårdspersonal som erbjuder SRH-tjänster inklusive vård till offer av sexuellt eller könsbaserat våld.

This contribution from Sweden will improve access to family planning services and modern contraceptives methods that build on a sustainable model of social marketing (to increase demand and uptake) in North and South Kivu provinces and the surrounding areas. DKT will strengthen the province's distribution system to ensure a permanent presence of contraceptive and Post Abortion Care as well as Medical Abortion products. Through the program, community-based providers will be trained and empowered to work within their communities to educate women and men on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR). Health care providers will also be trained to serve survivors of gender-based violence (GBV) and address taboos around sexuality, and family/community influences on family size. The goal is to strengthen national ownership and the long-term sustainability of reproductive health care, including abortion and GBV care in the DRC.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
The DKT bilateral program in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) aims to expand access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) services, strengthen prevention of gender based violence (GBV) and ensure comprehensive care capacity, and promote sustainable delivery through the community based Bee outreach model.
In 2024, following the termination of the regional DKT component due to budget reductions, the Embassy extended the bilateral program by one year (January-December 2026) through a costed contract amendment. An additional SEK 9,600,000 was reallocated from the discontinued regional program to the bilateral program to minimize the negative impact of the cuts, especially on supply availability and service continuity.
The program implementation period was January to December each year, however, due to delays in finalizing the new agreement in 2024, and corresponding disbursement, the first installment (SEK 10 million) was not paid until November 2024. This resulted in significant delays in implementation. In consultation with DKT, the programs original 12 month timeline for 2024-2025 was revised to 14 months, covering 1 November 2024 to 31 December 2025.
Another major shift involved the temporary reallocation of program activities from North and South Kivu, initial focus areas due to escalating insecurity, to more stable provinces of Tshopo and Congo Central. This adjustment was proposed by DKT and approved by the Embassy on 25 March 2025. The programs core objectives remain unchanged: - Expanding access to SRHR commodities and services - Empowering communitybased service providers (Bees) - Strengthening GBV and comprehensive abortion care (CAC) services - Promoting longterm sustainability through Bee cooperatives
Key adjustments include: - Reduced activities in volatile provinces - New performance targets in safer areas - Revised training and clinic support targets -Reallocation of training funds toward social marketing and awareness campaigns -Stronger media and digital engagement focus -Phased activities for demand generation, training, and RM&E (Results Monitoring & Evaluation)
Training budget was partially redirected to awareness campaigns. While this shift is justified within the current context, it should be noted that training tends to yield more sustainable long term outcomes. This tradeoff should be monitored closely going forward.
A field monitoring mission was conducted in Kinshasa on 17 July 2025, where four pharmacies and three health clinics collaborating with DKT were visited: Pharmacies were wellstocked with DKTsupported SRHR products such as OK Condoms, NorLevo emergency contraceptives, lubricants, and implants. Clinics visited included: Christina Clinic and Victoria Medical Center. Service availability and visibility were assessed positively.
Additionally, four active Bee agents were interviewed. They reported making 10 12 household visits per day, offering SRHR counselling and referring clients to clinics and hospitals. This model remains a strong pillar of the programs demand generation strategy.
The program includes a structured risk analysis, including three security scenarios with matching budget allocations. While generally well developed, several areas need strengthening: Mitigation planning in newly added provinces could be more detailed Supply chain risks including delays in procurement and transport, remain a concern Staff retention and safety in volatile provinces needs long-term consideration.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
